title: Ramayana Releases English Trailer With AI Lip-Sync as Diwali Debut Nears
excerpt: The makers of India's most expensive film use AI-powered dubbing technology for the English trailer, signaling a global push ahead of the November 6 release.
body:
• The English version of the Ramayana trailer, featuring AI-driven lip-sync technology, was released on August 5, marking the first Indian film to use automated lip-syncing for international audiences.
  • Ramayana: Part 1 is set for a worldwide theatrical release on November 6, 2026, during the Diwali weekend, with Part 2 planned for October 2027.
  • The film carries a reported budget of around $500 million, making it one of the most expensive Indian productions ever, with music by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.
  • Dharma Productions acquired North Indian distribution rights for around ₹250 crore, while Sony Pictures Entertainment secured overseas theatrical distribution.

An English Trailer Built by AI

The makers of Ramayana released an English version of the film's trailer on August 5, using AI-powered lip-sync technology to match the actors' mouth movements to English dialogue. The result is a trailer where Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash appear to speak English natively — a first for an Indian film of this scale.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=74nF-FWAS6M

The original Hindi trailer, released digitally on July 30 after an exclusive screening at New Delhi's Bharat Mandapam on July 18, had already generated enormous buzz. It was also showcased at San Diego Comic-Con on July 23, where Kapoor and Yash received a standing ovation from a Hall H crowd more accustomed to Marvel and DC presentations.

"I've always been a fan of comic conventions. To finally be here on the other side with a story, which is so ingrained in our culture, to bring that to a larger audience, it's really a proud moment for our entire team."

— Ranbir Kapoor, at San Diego Comic-Con

A Global Release Strategy

The AI lip-sync approach signals the scale of the global ambitions behind Ramayana. The film is planned to be visually dubbed into multiple languages including English, Spanish, and Japanese, according to Wikipedia's documentation of the production. Sony Pictures Entertainment has acquired overseas theatrical distribution rights, positioning it for a wide international rollout.

Domestically, Dharma Productions picked up the North Indian distribution rights for a reported ₹250 crore, reflecting the film's box office expectations. The first installment will release during Diwali on November 6, 2026, in standard and IMAX formats, with Part 2 slated for Diwali 2027.

The Cast and the Scale

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari of Dangal and Chhichhore fame, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Kannada superstar Yash as Ravana. The supporting cast includes Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, Arun Govil — who played Rama in the iconic 1987 TV series — as King Dashrath, and Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi.

The film's musical score comes from an unprecedented collaboration between Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman, while action sequences were choreographed by Hollywood veterans Terry Notary and Guy Norris. The visual effects are handled by eight-time Academy Award-winning studio DNEG, led by producer Namit Malhotra.

"I think this is the right kind of crowd who really understand the nuances of this kind of film and the effort that goes behind it. If they're excited, they're the most important people."

— Yash, at San Diego Comic-Con

What to Expect

The trailer reveals key moments from the epic — the wedding of Rama and Sita, their 14-year exile from Ayodhya, and the abduction of Sita by Ravana. With a reported budget of around $500 million, Ramayana is being positioned as India's answer to The Lord of the Rings — an epic that can travel globally while staying rooted in Indian mythology.

At CinemaCon 2026 in Los Angeles, producer Malhotra compared the film's ambitions to blending elements of fantasy and human drama from The Lord of the Rings and Gladiator. Whether that comparison holds will become clear on November 6.
nri_angle: The AI lip-sync English trailer marks an unprecedented global push for an Indian film, with Sony handling overseas distribution to bring the epic to diaspora audiences worldwide.
